title: Rethinking Data Selection: The Importance of Coverage over Difficulty in LLM Fine-Tuning
abstract: arXiv:2611.07323v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Selecting high-quality training data can reduce computation cost for LLM fine-tuning. Prior work on data selection developed a variety of difficulty-based scores, motivated by the intuition that harder examples are more informative. While effective for smaller classification models, we find that such methods often fail to outperform random selection for LLM fine-tuning. Our analysis reveals that random selection performs better because it is more representative of the underlying input space---i.e., has better coverage. To validate the importance of coverage, we implement a simple clustering-based selection method which selects data that is more representative of the underlying input distribution. On a set of diverse single-domain tasks, this method yields performance at or above that of random selection. translated_title: 重新思考数据选择：在LLM微调中覆盖度比特难度更重要
translated_abstract: 选择高质量的训练数据可以降低LLM微调的计算成本。以往的数据选择研究基于“更难的样本信息量更大”这一直觉，开发了多种基于难度的评分方法。虽然这些方法对较小的分类模型有效，但我们发现它们在LLM微调中往往无法超越随机选择。我们的分析揭示，随机选择表现更好的原因是它更能代表潜在的输入空间——即具有更好的覆盖度。为了验证覆盖度的重要性，我们实现了一种简单的基于聚类的选择方法，该方法选择更能代表潜在输入分布的数据。在一系列多样化的单领域任务上，该方法达到了与随机选择相当或更好的性能。在多样化、多领域的Tülu 3混合数据集上（此时随机采样不再能保证子集的均衡性），我们的方法优于随机选择。
tldr: 该研究发现在LLM微调的数据选择中，数据对输入分布的覆盖度比样本难度更重要，并提出一种简单的基于聚类的选择方法，在单领域任务上与随机选择持平，在多领域数据集上优于随机选择。
en_tdlr: Coverage of the input distribution matters more than example difficulty for LLM fine-tuning data selection; a simple clustering-based selection method matches random selection on single-domain tasks and outperforms it on multi-domain mixtures.
